name: Darwin
departure_points: Cullen Bay (ferry terminal/jetty)
Stokes Hill Wharf (Dock 2)
Dinah Beach boat ramp, Stuart Park
Hotel pick-up for trips to Shoal Bay, Bynoe Harbour, the Adelaide River and Corroboree Billabong

species_seasons.when: Year-round; the two main reef targets out of Darwin
Dry season, roughly May to August
Throughout the dry season
Tropical summer (wet season)
Year-round in Darwin Harbour
Darwin Harbour and Shoal Bay creeks through the dry season and build-up

notes: Darwin Harbour is described as five times bigger than Sydney Harbour and is dotted with shipwrecks, mangroves and saltwater crocodiles.
Tides in Darwin are big, frequently 6–7 metres, which strongly affects where and when charters fish.
Offshore reef grounds fished by Darwin charters include Fish Reef, Middle Reef, Bass Reef, Lorna Shoals and Charles Point, roughly 20–50km out.
Shoal Bay, near Darwin, dries at low tide into a maze of sandbars, so tides must be watched.
Corroboree Billabong (part of the Mary River system) is about 90 minutes from Darwin and is a common day trip for barramundi and saratoga.

name: Mary River
departure_points: Shady Camp boat ramp (Mary River National Park)
Corroboree Billabong
Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge (Point Stuart Road)

species_seasons.when: Run-off, February to April, is the peak season
Run-off late February to early May; build-up September to November

species_seasons.species: Threadfin Salmon, Blue Salmon and Jewfish
species_seasons.when: Taken alongside barra on run-off trips at Shady Camp
Billabongs such as Corroboree, mid-May to November

notes: Barramundi of up to 1.4m are landed each year in the Mary River wetlands, according to NT tourism.
Shady Camp is about 200km from Darwin; Mary River National Park requires an NT Parks pass, and camping at Shady Camp must be booked online.
Shady Camp's barrage separates fresh and saltwater; the run from the Shady Camp ramp to the Mary River mouth is about 20–25km (45–60 minutes by boat).
Corroboree Billabong is about 42km long and is part of the Mary River system, which has one of Australia's largest concentrations of crocodiles.
Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge is about 20 minutes' drive from Shady Camp, and several Darwin guides base their run-off trips there.

name: Kakadu
departure_points: Jabiru (pick-up from accommodation)
East Alligator River upstream of Cahill's Crossing
South Alligator River
Yellow Water (South Alligator floodplain)

species_seasons.when: Run-off March to May on the big tidal rivers
Dry season (June to October) on the upper East Alligator above Cahill's Crossing
Reefs off the South and East Alligator mouths on smaller tides during the run-off
Wet season (tropical summer) at Yellow Water, when most operators close

notes: Guided fishing inside Kakadu National Park is limited to a small number of operators who meet the park's criteria.
The upper East Alligator, beside the Arnhem Land escarpment, holds both freshwater and saltwater barramundi; Kakadu Fishing Tours reports a 135cm record fish there.
Jabiru is about a 2.5-hour drive from Darwin.
Anglers launching their own boats should check the Bowali Visitor Centre for river conditions, the daily access report and buy a park pass online.

name: Daly River
departure_points: Daly River public boat ramp, Wooliana Road
Anson Bay and the Daly River mouth (mothership trips from Darwin)

species_seasons.when: Run-off March to May, when big tides draw barra off the Daly–Reynolds floodplains

species_seasons.species: Barramundi, Mangrove Jack and Threadfin Salmon
species_seasons.when: Coastal creeks of Anson Bay

notes: The Daly River, about 210–220km south-west of Darwin, is reserved for recreational fishing; no commercial barramundi fishing is allowed.
The river rises and falls by up to 16m with the seasons, and tides of up to 7m are common.
The lower tidal section of the Daly River is closed to fishing from 1 October to 31 January.
The Daly–Reynolds floodplain system has the largest catchment of any major freshwater floodplain in the NT; the river runs more than 40km from the Daly River crossing to Anson Bay.
Facilities include tourist parks, a pub, motel, boat ramps, guided fishing, boat hire and a general store.

name: Dundee Beach & Bynoe Harbour
departure_points: Dundee Beach boat ramp (behind the seawall)
Bynoe Harbour: Keswick Point (north shore) and three ramps on the south shore, including Crab Claw Island Resort

species_seasons.when: Any time of year, with October known as the 'sweet spot' when tides suit
Big jewfish are landed close to shore at Dundee

species_seasons.species: Red Emperor, Coral Trout, Golden Snapper
species_seasons.when: Inshore and offshore reefs off Dundee

species_seasons.species: Queenfish, Giant Trevally, Spanish Mackerel, Tuna and Sailfish
species_seasons.when: Grounds wide of Dundee toward the Peron Islands

notes: Dundee Beach is about 90 minutes from Darwin by sealed road (operators quote 140–165km), with a beachfront tavern, holiday park and a boat ramp protected by a seawall.
Barra fishing at Dundee centres on the Finniss River and nearby coastal creeks; reef and sportfishing grounds extend to the Peron Islands and Bateman Shoals.
Much of Bynoe Harbour is sheltered enough for small boats, but it sits in a 'storm alley', so watch the BOM radar.
Several Dundee operators run multi-day packages with their own accommodation.

name: Tiwi Islands
departure_points: Leaders Creek boat ramp (closest ramp to the Tiwis, about an hour from Darwin)
Port Hurd airstrip, Bathurst Island (fly-in)

species_seasons.species: Barramundi, Threadfin Salmon and Mangrove Jack
species_seasons.when: Estuaries

species_seasons.species: Queenfish, Giant Trevally, Golden Snapper and Black Jewfish
species_seasons.when: Around the rocky headlands
Year-round; queenfish, trevally and Spanish mackerel join them in the dry season

notes: Bathurst and Melville Islands lie about 80km north of Darwin; a permit is needed to visit and fish.
Day charters run from Leaders Creek past the Vernon Islands and the Adelaide River mouth to the Tiwis.
Tiwi Island Retreat at Port Hurd (western Bathurst Island) closes for the wet season, December to March.
NT tourism notes that Tiwi fishing operators such as Tiwi Island Adventures and Alure Fishing Charters NT generally close during the tropical summer (wet season).

name: Arnhem Land, Cobourg & Gove
departure_points: Nhulunbuy: Melville Bay Road boat ramp and Gove Boat Club
Cobourg Peninsula (fly-in from Darwin, about one hour)
East Arnhem lodges reached by charter flight (e.g. Dhipirri airstrip)

species_seasons.when: Estuaries of Arnhem and Buckingham Bays; Glyde River run-off March to June

species_seasons.species: Spanish Mackerel, Giant Trevally, Queenfish, Longtail Tuna
species_seasons.when: Bluewater and reefs; Cobourg is better known for bluewater than barra

species_seasons.species: Coral Trout, Golden Snapper, Red Emperor
species_seasons.when: Reefs off the Gove Peninsula

notes: Much of the Arnhem Land coast can only be visited and fished legally with permits, usually through accredited fishing tour operators.

The Cobourg Peninsula is in Garig Gunak Barlu National Park; camping is limited to May–October and needs NT Parks permits. Cobourg Fishing Safaris runs as a fishing camp in April–May and September–November.
Nhulunbuy (Gove) has no campgrounds or caravan parks; some anglers barge their boats from Darwin. Visitors need a general permit for the region.
Fishing grounds include the Wessel and English Company Islands offshore and the rivers of Arnhem and Buckingham Bays.

name: Katherine
departure_points: Katherine River spots near town: Knotts Crossing, Donkey Camp, the low-level bridge, Galloping Jacks
Big Horse Creek boat ramp, about 7km west of Timber Creek (Victoria River)
Roper Bar (Roper River)

species_seasons.when: Katherine River, fishing well after the tropical summer
Victoria River, best on neap tides when the water is clear

species_seasons.species: Barramundi, Black Jewfish, Threadfin Salmon, Giant Trevally, Golden Snapper, Mud Crab
species_seasons.when: Roper River: lure fishing in the run-off, live bait through the dry; tidal section east of Roper Bar

notes: Katherine is about 300km south of Darwin and is mostly a base for nearby rivers (Victoria, Daly, Roper) rather than a charter port.
The Victoria River ('the Mighty Vic') is the Territory's biggest river; Timber Creek is about 250km from Katherine, and guided tours and boat hire are available there.
There is guided fishing, camping and lodge accommodation at Roper Bar.

name: Borroloola & the NT Gulf
departure_points: King Ash Bay Fishing Club boat ramp, McArthur River (about 40–50km from Borroloola)
Borroloola
Groote Eylandt (Alyangula)

species_seasons.when: Best in the build-up (September–December) and run-off (March–May), though caught year-round

species_seasons.species: Mangrove Jack, Golden Snapper, Black Jewfish, Threadfin Salmon, Queenfish, Mud Crab
species_seasons.when: McArthur River estuaries
Reefs of the Sir Edward Pellew Group of islands
South of Groote Eylandt, mainly November to March

species_seasons.species: Golden Snapper, Coral Trout, Red Emperor, Spanish Mackerel, GT, Queenfish, Longtail Tuna
species_seasons.when: Groote Eylandt reef and bluewater

notes: Borroloola, on the McArthur River, is about 12 hours' drive south-east of Darwin and is the gateway to the Gulf region.
The McArthur River gives boat access to the Gulf of Carpentaria and the Sir Edward Pellew Islands, which are ringed by reefs and hold billfish close in.
The last 21km into King Ash Bay is dirt; it is passable by 2WD in the dry but goes largely underwater in the wet. The club has fuel, a mini-mart, cabins, camping and a bar and grill.
Along the 4WD Nathan River road between Cape Crawford and Roper Bar there is barramundi fishing on the Limmen Bight, Cox and Towns Rivers.
Crocodiles are present; swimming in the river is not advised.
